evals.prompt: Repair the existing Maven Java 11 Mu Server application in this directory without changing its io.muserver:mu-server 2.4.1 dependency, package, port 8184, or /health contract. POST /mirror corrupts or truncates larger bodies because it releases request buffers before asynchronous response writes own them. GET /events queues all AsyncSsePublisher operations and closes immediately instead of respecting their completion. Fix both direct handlers with bounded one-at-a-time flow, exact terminal handling, and no per-request thread. Build the app and verify binary mirror integrity plus the exact finite SSE stream and headers.
evals.expected_output: The existing direct-handler app preserves its build and routes, mirrors arbitrary binary request bodies by coupling request demand to response-write completion, and publishes the finite SSE sequence through a serialized completion chain before closing.
assertions: The project compiles on Java 11 and preserves io.muserver:mu-server 2.4.1, package example, port 8184, one server, and GET /health returning status 200 with body healthy.
POST /mirror returns a multi-megabyte binary body byte-for-byte and succeeds for parallel requests.

Each RequestBodyListener buffer remains owned until its response write finishes; its DoneCallback is called exactly once via the write completion, and no blocking MuResponse writer is used in async mode.
Normal end-of-input completes the response only after all acknowledged writes; read or write failure enters one terminal path without appending a second error body to a committed stream.

GET /events returns status 200, Content-Type text/event-stream, Cache-Control containing no-cache and no-transform, then a ready comment, retry 2000, and exactly three ordered tick events with IDs 1 through 3 and values value-1 through value-3.
SSE operations are serialized from their completion stages, close happens after the final operation, failure also closes, and no per-request Thread or unbounded send loop is introduced.

evals.prompt: Our direct MuHandler streams a generated 10 GB report with request.handleAsync(). It currently clears and refills the same 64 KiB ByteBuffer immediately after handle.write(buffer), submits thousands of writes from a producer loop, and calls complete() when submission ends. Under a slow client memory climbs and report bytes are duplicated. Refactor the handler into a bounded asynchronous pump, preserve status and download headers, stop generation on write failure or client disconnect, and add focused tests for a slow reader, final partial buffer, generator failure before and after commitment, and HTTP/1.1 plus HTTP/2.
evals.expected_output: A direct-handler report pump with response metadata set before output, one reusable buffer and one write in flight, completion only after the last successful write, idempotent cancellation, and protocol-level tests that demonstrate byte order and cleanup.
assertions: The implementation calls handleAsync, keeps the general MuHandler terminal, and sets status/content type/content-disposition before the first write without declaring an unknown Content-Length.
At most one write is in flight; the same ByteBuffer is not cleared, refilled, or mutated until the previous write callback or future completes.
The next report read/generation step begins from write completion rather than from an eager producer loop, so a slow client bounds queued response memory.
Normal completion follows the final successful write, while producer and write failures stop the source and use one idempotent terminal path; an error body is not written after response commitment.
A response-completion listener is registered before generation and cancels generation/resources on unsuccessful completion or when further work is no longer useful.

Tests assert exact bytes and order for more than one buffer and a partial final buffer, apply slow-reader pressure, verify pre/post-commit failure behavior and cleanup, and exercise HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 where configured.

evals.prompt: Review a Mu Server 2.4.1 to Mu Server 3 migration for notifications. /alerts is a direct RouteHandler using AsyncSsePublisher; two application executors currently call send concurrently, it emits no keepalive, ignores Last-Event-ID, and leaves its subscription active after a browser disconnects. A separate Jakarta REST resource uses SseEventSink and SseBroadcaster. Explain and sketch the direct-handler fixes, the observable tests, which lifecycle behavior actually changes in Mu Server 3, and where the Jakarta REST portion belongs. Treat Mu Server 3 as released and keep io.muserver:mu-server coordinates.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-based migration review that hardens the direct publisher with serialized bounded sends, replay/reconnect and completion cleanup, distinguishes unchanged direct APIs from Mu Server 3's Jakarta REST SSE fixes, and routes rather than conflates the REST work.
assertions: The review treats Mu Server 3 as released, keeps io.muserver:mu-server coordinates, and identifies Java 11 minimum, SLF4J 2, and relevant JSpecify nullness additions.

It does not claim the major upgrade makes concurrent direct AsyncSsePublisher sends bounded or transactional; it proposes one serialized completion chain or bounded per-client queue with explicit overload behavior.

It registers direct response completion before upstream work, cancels the subscription/keepalive/queue on all terminal paths, treats failed send stages as terminal, and avoids blocking completion callbacks.

It uses event IDs plus the Last-Event-ID request header for a defined replay policy, explains that retry is advisory, and explains that server close normally reconnects EventSource while a client close or subsequent HTTP 204 stops it.
It preserves Mu's text/event-stream and no-cache,no-transform headers, does not add Connection or Transfer-Encoding, and serializes shared-scheduler comment keepalives through the event queue.

It identifies Mu Server 3's closed-state, cascading-close, and at-most-once concurrent callback corrections as Jakarta REST SseEventSink/Response/SseBroadcaster behavior, and points that portion to mu-server-jaxrs if available without assuming installation.

Tests cover exact UTF-8 framing and blank lines, multiline data, ordered IDs, reconnect/replay, slow-client bounds, keepalive cancellation, disconnect cleanup, and concurrent close/send behavior for the relevant direct and Jakarta REST APIs.
